# Open in WordPress Studio button

The Open in WordPress Studio button lets users spin up a new WordPress Studio site from a Blueprint with a single click.

When someone clicks the button or link, WordPress Studio launches on their machine (if installed) and opens the **Add site** dialog with the [Blueprint](https://wordpress.studio/docs/blueprints/) you provide, ready to create a new site from it. If they don’t have WordPress Studio installed, they’re sent to [the WordPress Studio landing page](https://wordpress.studio/) to download the app. Once installed, click the button again to launch the site.

You can embed Open in WordPress Studio buttons and links anywhere you share your work: GitHub repositories, plugin or theme listings, documentation, YouTube descriptions, and more. It’s a quick way to help users start working in WordPress Studio with your recommended setup.

Here’s an example that creates a new site in WordPress Studio with a Blueprint built for WordPress plugin and theme development.

[Open in WordPress Studio](https://wp.com/open?deep_link=add-site%3Fblueprint%%%253D)

## [Generate your own](#0-generate-your-own)

Use the [Open in WordPress Studio button generator](https://wordpress.studio/blueprint-button/) to build your own button or link. Paste any publicly accessible Blueprint URL, Base64 encoded JSON, or raw JSON, then copy the link as Markdown, HTML, or a URL. If you haven’t created a Blueprint before, see the [Blueprint guide](https://wordpress.studio/docs/blueprints/how-to-create-custom-blueprints/) for how to create one.

To build the link yourself, put a Blueprint URL in the `blueprint_url` parameter, or the Blueprint JSON encoded as Base64 in the `blueprint` parameter, of an `add-site` deep link. Then URL-encode that deep link into a `wp.com/open` link:

```
https://wp.com/open?deep_link=add-site%3Fblueprint_url%3D<URL-encoded Blueprint URL>
```

Use a Blueprint URL for a setup you keep updating, such as a file in your GitHub repository: the link always opens its latest version. Use Base64 JSON for a fixed setup with no file to host.
